items.title: Newtonian comparison momentum and kinetic energy in a named inertial frame
items.reference: scaffold/special-relativity.md SR11 reservation ("pthm specified p/E correspondence"); scaffold/mathematical-prerequisites.md#M08
items.design_state: definition introducing the comparison functionals the specified p/E correspondence is stated against; no approximation is asserted here
items.physical_scope: Formulation definition inside the flat special-relativity framework: the Newtonian comparison momentum and kinetic energy are built from a named inertial frame, its spatial Euclidean structure, a positive mass parameter and a coordinate velocity, in the SI conventions of the framework. The definition asserts no approximation, correspondence or error bound, no Newtonian theory, no force or matter law, and no empirical content; the correspondence claim is pthm-sr-newtonian-p-e-correspondence.
items.statement:
Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski model ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]), let $c>0$ with the SI conventions of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]], let $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ be an inertial frame with inertial chart $x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ and spatial Euclidean structure $(S,\delta,|\cdot|)$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]), and let $m>0$.

(a) For $w\in S$ define the *Newtonian comparison momentum* and the *Newtonian comparison kinetic energy* of the pair $(m,w)$ by $$N_p(m,w):=mw,\qquad N_K(m,w):=\tfrac12\,m\,|w|^2,$$ where $mw$ is the scalar multiple of $w$ by the real number $m$ ([[def-linear-map]]) and $|w|^2=\delta(w,w)$ ([[def-integer-power]]). With the SI conventions these carry the units kilogram metre per second and joule respectively.

(b) Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval ([[def-interval]]) and let $y:I\to A$ have inertial coordinate path $t\mapsto(ct,r(t))$; writing $r(t)=r^1(t)e_1+r^2(t)e_2+r^3(t)e_3$ with real functions $r^1,r^2,r^3$, at each parameter value $t$ where all three coordinate derivatives exist, define the *coordinate velocity* $w(t)\in S$ of the path by $$w(t):=(r^1)'(t)\,e_1+(r^2)'(t)\,e_2+(r^3)'(t)\,e_3,$$ the componentwise derivative of [[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]]. For a path differentiable at every parameter value these are functions on $I$; otherwise they are defined on its differentiability set. The comparison functionals along the path are $t\mapsto N_p(m,w(t))$ and $t\mapsto N_K(m,w(t))$.

(c) The functionals $N_p$ and $N_K$ are comparison expressions built from a named inertial frame, the mass parameter $m$ and the path's coordinate velocity. They are not defined by, and do not presuppose, a separately developed Newtonian theory, and this definition asserts no approximation, correspondence, error bound or physical claim; those are the content of [[pthm-sr-newtonian-p-e-correspondence]].
items.strategy: A definition item. Well-definedness: clause (a) applies the scalar multiple of a vector of the real vector space $V$ (restricted to $S\subseteq V$) and the square of the norm $|\cdot|$ supplied by the frame's spatial structure, both total on $S$; clause (b) uses the componentwise derivative of a function $I\to\mathbb R^3$ and the unique expansion of a vector of $S$ in the ordered basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of [[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]. No division occurs and no choice is used. The definition deliberately introduces no physical correspondence: it only names the two expressions that [[pthm-sr-newtonian-p-e-correspondence]] compares with the model's measured quantities, and the units are the ones fixed by [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]]. The derivative symbols in(b) are used only at points where the coordinate derivatives exist; no velocity is assigned to an arbitrary nondifferentiable path. Physical correspondence consumers retain their stated differentiable future-timelike worldline hypotheses.

references.title: B. Crowell, Special Relativity, revision 2020-12-10 (author-published undergraduate textbook, 246 PDF pages); signature (+---) converted to (-+++) and c = 1 formulas restored to x^0 = c t; Section 4.2 pp. 82-86 (relativistic kinetic energy; Example 5 p. 86, the Newtonian prediction eV = (1/2)mv^2), Section 4.3.3 Example 8 p. 91 (the Newtonian limit v = p/m), Section 4.3.4 pp. 95-96 (p = m gamma v; the momentum of a material particle approaches infinity as its speed approaches c) and problems 11-12 p. 117 (expand K = m(gamma-1) and p = m gamma v in Taylor series; show the first terms are the nonrelativistic expressions)

S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997); signature (-+++) with c = 1. Chapter 1 Section 1.5 printed p. 27 (PDF p. 34): for small v, p^0 = m + (1/2)mv^2 (rest energy plus kinetic energy) and p^1 = mv (Newtonian momentum); Chapter 4 Section 4.1 printed pp. 105-106 (PDF pp. 112-113): the Newtonian limit, the slow-motion condition (4.10) and the weak static field

items.title: The uniform second-order Taylor remainder of $z\mapsto(1-z)^{-1/2}$ on $[0,z_0]$
items.reference: scaffold/mathematical-prerequisites.md#M08 ("Taylor with bounded second derivative"; constants depend on z_0); audit-expansion-report.md M08 branch
items.design_state: complete elementary argument from the published Lagrange-remainder supplier with an explicit uniform constant
items.statement:
Let $z_0\in[0,1)$ and define $f:(-\infty,1)\to\mathbb R$ by $f(z):=(1-z)^{-1/2}=\bigl((1-z)^{1/2}\bigr)^{-1}$, the reciprocal of the nonnegative square root, with rational powers as in [[def-rational-power]]; put $K(z_0):=\tfrac38(1-z_0)^{-5/2}$.

(a) $f$ is differentiable on $(-\infty,1)$ with $f'(z)=\tfrac12(1-z)^{-3/2}$, and twice differentiable there with $f''(z)=\tfrac34(1-z)^{-5/2}$; in particular $|f''(z)|\le\tfrac34(1-z_0)^{-5/2}$ for every $z\in[0,z_0]$.

(b) For every $z\in[0,z_0]$ there is a real $R(z)$ with $$f(z)=1+\tfrac z2+R(z),\qquad |R(z)|\le K(z_0)\,z^2,$$ so $|f(z)-1|\le\tfrac z2+K(z_0)z^2$ for $z\in[0,z_0]$. Consequently, for every $\eta>0$, $$0\le z\le\min\!\left\{z_0,\frac{\eta}{\tfrac12+K(z_0)z_0}\right\}\ \Longrightarrow\ |f(z)-1|\le\eta ;$$ the display is the quantitative form of $f(z)\to1$ as $z\to0^+$ used by [[lem-sr-uniform-galilean-limit-of-boost-charts]].

The lemma is a statement of real analysis about the single function $f$; it attaches no physical meaning to $z$ and makes no claim about a Lorentz factor or a physical velocity.
items.strategy:
(a) Write $f(z)=g(1-z)^{-1}$ with $g(y):=y^{1/2}$ for $y>0$, or directly apply the power rule: by [[thm-real-power-agrees-with-rational-exponent]] the rational powers of [[def-rational-power]] agree on rational exponents with the real powers differentiated in [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]], whose second clause gives $(x^{\alpha})'=\alpha x^{\alpha-1}$ on $(0,\infty)$; the affine map $z\mapsto 1-z$ has derivative the constant $-1$ (identity and sum rules, [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[lem-derivative-of-a-power]]), so the chain rule [[thm-chain-rule]] applied to $z\mapsto(1-z)^{-1/2}=y^{\alpha}\circ(1-z)$ with $\alpha=-1/2$ gives $f'(z)=-\tfrac12(1-z)^{-3/2}\cdot(-1)=\tfrac12(1-z)^{-3/2}$, and repeating with $\alpha=-3/2$ gives $f''(z)=\tfrac34(1-z)^{-5/2}$; the identities $(1-z)^{\alpha}(1-z)^{-\alpha}=1$ and $a^{-r}=(a^r)^{-1}$ are [[lem-rational-power-laws]]. For the bound: from $0\le z\le z_0$ we have $0<1-z_0\le1-z$, so positive-base $5/2$-power monotonicity in the base of [[lem-rational-power-monotone]] with $r=5/2$ gives $(1-z_0)^{5/2}\le(1-z)^{5/2}$ (equality exactly when $z=z_0$, by the strict part otherwise), and [[lem-of-inverse-positive]] gives $(1-z)^{-5/2}\le(1-z_0)^{-5/2}$; multiplying by $\tfrac34$ and reading $|f''|=f''$ (the strict positivity of the power, [[lem-rational-power-laws]] clause 1) gives the claim.

(b) Put $n=1$, $a=0$, $x=z\in[0,z_0]$ in [[cor-taylor-remainder-bound]]: $f$ has derivatives through order $2$ on the closed interval between $0$ and $z$ with endpoint continuity (indeed it is $C^{\infty}$ on the open neighbourhood $(-\infty,1)$ of that interval), and $|f''(t)|\le\tfrac34(1-z_0)^{-5/2}=:M$ there by (a); hence $|R_{1,0}f(z)|\le M z^2/2!=K(z_0)z^2$ for $R(z):=R_{1,0}f(z)=f(z)-f(0)-f'(0)z=f(z)-1-\tfrac z2$. The final display follows from $|f(z)-1|\le z(\tfrac12+K(z_0)z)\le z(\tfrac12+K(z_0)z_0)$ for $z\le z_0$ and the order arithmetic of $\mathbb R$ with the absolute-value properties of [[lem-of-abs-value]] ([[def-abs-value]]). The final implication explicitly retains z<=z0; its bound is not asserted beyond the original Taylor interval. At z0=0 it applies only to z=0, while the one-sided convergence statement may use any fixed positive z0<1.

references.title: J. Lebl, Basic Analysis I: Introduction to Real Analysis, Volume I, Section 5.4 "Taylor's theorem" (Taylor's theorem with the Lagrange remainder and its error estimate)
MIT OpenCourseWare 18.100B Real Analysis, Spring 2025 full lecture notes (Taylor's theorem, the Lagrange remainder and the differentiation rules)

items.title: Uniform low-speed expansion of the observer energy, momentum and kinetic energy of a massive four-momentum
items.design_state: complete transport of the Taylor remainder through the mass-shell identities with uniform constants depending only on the speed bound
items.statement:
Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski model ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]), $c>0$, let $n\in V$ be future unit with $\eta(n,n)=-1$, and let $P=mU$ with $m>0$ and $U\in V$ future timelike, $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$. Let $E_n(P)$, $q_n(P)$, $T_n(P)$ and $m(P)$ be the observer energy, spatial momentum, kinetic energy and invariant mass of [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]], put $h(v):=v+\eta(n,v)n$ as in [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]](c), and let $\gamma:=-\eta(U/c,n)\ge1$ and $w:=h(U)/\gamma=c\,h(U/c)/\gamma\in n^\perp$ be the Lorentz factor and relative velocity of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(d); then $u:=U/c$ satisfies $u=\gamma(n+w/c)$, $|w|^2=c^2(1-\gamma^{-2})$ and $\gamma=(1-|w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$, and [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(b) gives $E_n(P)=mc^2\gamma$, $q_n(P)=m\gamma w$, $T_n(P)=mc^2(\gamma-1)$ and $m(P)=m$.

Let $z_0\in[0,1)$, suppose $z:=|w|^2/c^2\le z_0$, put $K(z_0):=\tfrac38(1-z_0)^{-5/2}$, and let $f,R$ be as in [[lem-sr-uniform-low-speed-taylor-remainder]], so that $\gamma=f(z)$ and $\gamma=1+\tfrac z2+R(z)$ with $|R(z)|\le K(z_0)z^2$. Then:

(a) $E_n(P)=mc^2+\tfrac12m|w|^2+R_E$ and $T_n(P)=\tfrac12m|w|^2+R_E$ for the common real number $R_E:=mc^2R(z)$, and $$|R_E|\le K(z_0)\,z\,m|w|^2=K(z_0)\,\frac{m|w|^4}{c^2},\qquad \Bigl|T_n(P)-\tfrac12m|w|^2\Bigr|\le 2K(z_0)\,z\,\tfrac12m|w|^2 .$$

(b) $q_n(P)=mw+R_q$ with $R_q:=m(\gamma-1)w$, and $$|R_q|\le m|w|\Bigl(\frac z2+K(z_0)z^2\Bigr)\le\Bigl(\frac12+K(z_0)z_0\Bigr)z\,m|w| ;$$ moreover $|q_n(P)|=mc\sqrt{\gamma^2-1}=m\gamma|w|$ and $m(P)=m$.

(c) Every constant above depends only on $z_0$, so the estimates are uniform over all future unit $n$, all $m>0$ and all $P=mU$ with $|w|^2\le z_0c^2$; if $z=0$ (equivalently $w=0$, $U=cn$) then $R_E=R_q=0$, $E_n(P)=mc^2$, $q_n(P)=0$ and $T_n(P)=0$. The lemma is a statement about the mathematical model only; it asserts no measured quantity, no approximation of a physical theory and no error estimate for any experiment.
items.strategy:
First use the linearity of h in thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition(c): h(U)=c h(U/c), so w=h(U)/gamma=c h(u)/gamma for u=U/c. The future-unit u has gamma=−eta(n,u), and the actual supplier(d) then gives u=gamma(n+w/c), |w|²=c²(1−gamma^−2) and gamma=f(z). No extra factor c multiplies h(U)/gamma. Combine [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(b), [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(d) and [[lem-sr-uniform-low-speed-taylor-remainder]]. Since $z=|w|^2/c^2$, clause (d) of the theorem gives $\gamma=(1-|w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}=(1-z)^{-1/2}=f(z)$, hence $\gamma-1=\tfrac z2+R(z)$ with $|R(z)|\le K(z_0)z^2$.

(a) Multiply by $mc^2$: $E_n(P)=mc^2\gamma=mc^2+\tfrac12m|w|^2+mc^2R(z)$, because $mc^2\cdot\tfrac z2=\tfrac12mc^2z=\tfrac12m|w|^2$; and $T_n(P)=E_n(P)-mc^2$ by [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]]\,(b), so the same remainder occurs. The bound $|mc^2R(z)|\le mc^2K(z_0)z^2=K(z_0)zm|w|^2$ gives the first display, and $2K(z_0)z\cdot\tfrac12m|w|^2=K(z_0)zm|w|^2$ gives the second.

(b) $q_n(P)=m\gamma w=mw+m(\gamma-1)w$, and $|m(\gamma-1)w|=m|\gamma-1|\,|w|$ by the product rule for absolute values ([[lem-of-abs-value]], [[def-abs-value]]); substituting $\gamma-1=\tfrac z2+R(z)$ and $|R(z)|\le K(z_0)z^2$ gives $|R_q|\le m|w|(\tfrac z2+K(z_0)z^2)\le m|w|z(\tfrac12+K(z_0)z_0)$ because $z\le z_0$ and $m|w|,K(z_0)\ge0$; the norm identity is clause (b) of the batch-8 lemma and $m(P)=m$ is [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]]\,(b). The case $z=0$ is the vanishing of the remainders at the origin, $f(0)=1$.

items.title: Galilean limiting chart maps and bounded chart regions
items.reference: scaffold/special-relativity.md SR11 reservation ("explicit Galilean limiting chart maps with bounded domains")
items.design_state: definition of the family of affine chart maps whose bounded-region limit is proved in lem-sr-uniform-galilean-limit-of-boost-charts
items.statement:
Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski model and let $c>0$ be a fixed mathematical speed scale, with the coordinate convention $x^0=ct$, let $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ be an inertial frame with inertial chart $x$ and spatial Euclidean structure $(S,\delta,|\cdot|)$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]), and write the points of $\mathbb R\times S$ as $(t,x)$.

(a) *Lorentz boost charts with a variable speed scale.* For $v\in S$ and a real $C>|v|$ put $\gamma_C(v):=(1-|v|^2/C^2)^{-1/2}$ ([[def-rational-power]]) and define the affine map $\Phi_{v,C}:\mathbb R\times S\to\mathbb R\times S$ by $$\Phi_{v,C}(t,x):=\Bigl(\gamma_C(v)\bigl(t-\tfrac{\delta(v,x)}{C^2}\bigr),\ \ x+\tfrac{\gamma_C(v)-1}{|v|^2}\delta(v,x)\,v-\gamma_C(v)\,t\,v\Bigr)\quad(v\ne0),$$ with $\Phi_{0,C}:=\mathrm{id}$; when $|v|<c$, at $C=c$ this is the coordinate expression, in the convention $x^0=ct$, of the passive Lorentz boost $B(v/c)$ of [[def-lorentz-boost]]: if an event has coordinates $(ct,x)$ in the unprimed inertial chart of the frame, then $\Phi_{v,c}(t,x)$ are its coordinates $(x'^0/c,\,x'^1,x'^2,x'^3)$ in the boosted inertial chart with parameter $v/c$.

(b) *Galilean boost.* For $v\in S$ define the affine map $G_v:\mathbb R\times S\to\mathbb R\times S$ by $G_v(t,x):=(t,\,x-tv)$.

(c) *Bounded chart region.* For reals $T,R>0$ put $D_{T,R}:=\{(t,x)\in\mathbb R\times S:|t|\le T,\ |x|\le R\}$, with $|\cdot|$ the norm of the named frame.

(d) *Scope of the family.* The parameter $C$ is a variable speed scale inside a family of coordinate expressions; it is not a change of the model's adopted constant $c$, and the members with $C\ne c$ are auxiliary mathematical maps used only to state the limit of [[lem-sr-uniform-galilean-limit-of-boost-charts]]. Nothing here asserts a physical limit of the framework, and no limiting trajectory, force or interaction is defined.
items.strategy: A definition item. Well-definedness: for $v\ne0$, $C>|v|$ the number $\gamma_C(v)$ is a rational power of the positive base $1-|v|^2/C^2$ ([[def-rational-power]]), and the displayed formulas assign to each pair $(t,x)$ a pair of elements of $\mathbb R\times S$ using the bilinear form $\delta$ and scalar multiplication in $S$; for $v=0$ the middle term is $0/0$ and the map is declared separately to be the identity (the same convention as [[def-lorentz-boost]]). The identification at $C=c$ is made only when $|v|<c$, so this member belongs to the family; it is a substitution: writing $\beta:=v/c$ and $x^0:=ct$ in the definition of $B(\beta)$ of [[def-lorentz-boost]] gives $x'^0=\gamma(x^0-\beta\cdot x)$ and $x'=x+((\gamma-1)/|\beta|^2)(\beta\cdot x)\beta-\gamma\beta x^0$, that is $x'^0/c=\gamma_C(v)(t-\delta(v,x)/C^2)$ and the displayed spatial formula, because $\beta\cdot x=\delta(v,x)/c$, $|\beta|^2=|v|^2/c^2$ and $\beta x^0=(v/c)(ct)=vt$. The definition proves no uniform limit; the purely mathematical bounded-region limit is proved later. It assigns no physical interpretation to the auxiliary family, which varies C without changing the fixed model parameter c.

items.title: Uniform Galilean limit of the boost charts on bounded regions, and its failure on unbounded regions
items.reference: scaffold/special-relativity.md SR11 reservation ("explicit Galilean limiting chart maps with bounded domains"); prose-scaffold.md SR11 row (Carroll slow-motion discussion pp. 105-106)
items.design_state: complete explicit bound-and-limit argument on the bounded chart region from the pair's own definitions and the uniform Taylor remainder
items.statement:
Let $v\in S$, $T,R>0$, and let $(\Phi_{v,C})_{C>|v|}$, $G_v$ and $D_{T,R}$ be as in [[def-sr-galilean-limiting-charts]]. For $C>|v|$ write $\gamma_C:=(1-|v|^2/C^2)^{-1/2}$ and $z:=|v|^2/C^2$, and for $(t,x)\in\mathbb R\times S$ write $\Phi_{v,C}(t,x)=(t',x')$.

(a) *Exact differences.* For every $C>|v|$ and all $(t,x)$,
$$t'-t=(\gamma_C-1)t-\gamma_C\frac{\delta(v,x)}{C^2},\qquad x'-(x-tv)=(\gamma_C-1)(x_\parallel-tv),$$ where $x_\parallel:=\delta(v,x)v/|v|^2$ for $v\ne0$; for $v=0$ one has $\Phi_{0,C}=\mathrm{id}$ and both differences vanish.

(b) *Uniform bounds on bounded regions.* For every $v\ne0$, every $C>|v|$ and every $(t,x)\in D_{T,R}$,
$$|t'-t|\le(\gamma_C-1)T+\gamma_C\frac{|v|R}{C^2},\qquad |x'-(x-tv)|\le(\gamma_C-1)(R+|v|T).$$

(c) *Quantitative rate and uniform convergence to the Galilean chart map.* Fix $z_0\in(0,1)$ and set $K_0=\tfrac38(1-z_0)^{-5/2}$, $A_0=\tfrac12+K_0z_0$ and $\Gamma_0=(1-z_0)^{-1/2}$. Whenever $v\ne0$ and $C\ge |v|/\sqrt{z_0}$, the following hold uniformly on $D_{T,R}$: $$|t'-t|\le\frac{A_0|v|^2T+\Gamma_0|v|R}{C^2},\qquad |x'-(x-tv)|\le\frac{A_0|v|^2(R+|v|T)}{C^2}.$$ Thus the rate is $O(C^{-2})$ with explicit constants for fixed $v,T,R,z_0$. For every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $C_\varepsilon>|v|$ such that for every $C\ge C_\varepsilon$ and every $(t,x)\in D_{T,R}$, $$\max\{|t'-t|,\,|x'-(x-tv)|\}\le\varepsilon .$$ For $v\ne0$, put $H=T+R+|v|T$, choose any $z_1$ with $0<z_1\le\min\{z_0,(2A_0)^{-1},\varepsilon/(2A_0H)\}$ (for example the displayed minimum), and set $$C_\varepsilon=\max\{|v|/\sqrt{z_1},\sqrt{3|v|R/\varepsilon}\}.$$ This is sufficient, and since $z_1<1$ it gives $C_\varepsilon>|v|$. For $v=0$ both errors vanish identically and any $C_\varepsilon>0$ suffices. Hence $\sup_{D_{T,R}}\max\{|t'-t|,|x'-(x-tv)|\}\to0$ as $C\to\infty$ with $v,T,R$ fixed, the convergence is uniform on $D_{T,R}$, and for each fixed $(t,x)$ the image $\Phi_{v,C}(t,x)$ converges to the Galilean value $G_v(t,x)=(t,x-tv)$.

(d) *Failure on unbounded regions.* For every $v\ne0$ and every $C>|v|$, $\sup_{\mathbb R\times S}|t'-t|=+\infty$ and $\sup_{\mathbb R\times S}|x'-(x-tv)|=+\infty$; so the boundedness of $T,R$ in (c) is essential and the limit is not uniform on the whole chart domain.
items.strategy:
(a) Subtract the Galilean values from the definition: t'-t=(gamma_C-1)t-gamma_C delta(v,x)/C^2 and x'-(x-tv)=(gamma_C-1)(x_parallel-tv). For v=0 both maps are the identity and both differences vanish.

(b) Scalar absolute-value triangle inequality gives |t'-t|<=(gamma_C-1)|t|+gamma_C|delta(v,x)|/C^2. In a delta-orthonormal basis, thm-cauchy-schwarz-finite gives |delta(v,x)|<=|v||x|. The spatial inner-product norm's homogeneity and triangle inequality are cor-triangle-inequality-for-inner-product-norm: |x_parallel|=|delta(v,x)|/|v|<=|x|, hence |x_parallel-tv|<=|x_parallel|+|-tv|<=|x|+|t||v|. The absolute value of t is essential for negative chart times. Since gamma_C>=1, |t|<=T and |x|<=R, substitution proves both bounded-region displays.

(c) Fix z0 in (0,1). For 0<=z=|v|^2/C^2<=z0, the Taylor supplier's first remainder bound gives 0<=gamma_C-1<=z/2+K0 z^2<=A0 z. Positive-base rational-power monotonicity and reciprocal order give gamma_C<=(1-z0)^(-1/2)=Gamma0. Substitute into (b) to obtain both explicit C^-2 bounds. For epsilon>0, set H=T+R+|v|T>0 and choose 0<z1<=min{z0,1/(2A0),epsilon/(2A0H)}; each entry of the minimum is positive. For C>=|v|/sqrt(z1), z<=z1, so gamma_C-1<=A0 z1<=1/2 and (gamma_C-1)H<=epsilon/2. Thus gamma_C<=3/2. If also C>=sqrt(3|v|R/epsilon), the additional time term gamma_C|v|R/C^2<=epsilon/2, so both error bounds from (b) are <=epsilon on the whole bounded region. Because z1<=z0<1 and |v|>0, the first threshold is strictly larger than |v|; the inadmissible boost boundary C=|v| is excluded. For v=0 handle the identity family separately with any positive threshold. Supremum over the bounded region gives uniform convergence; each fixed point lies in such a region, giving pointwise convergence.

(d) For v nonzero and fixed C>|v|, gamma_C>1. At (t,x)=(0,lambda v/|v|), lambda>0, the spatial error norm is (gamma_C-1)lambda, unbounded as lambda increases. At (t,x)=(0,-mu v), mu>0, the time error is gamma_C mu |v|^2/C^2, unbounded as mu increases. Thus both whole-domain suprema are infinite. This is a coordinate-family limit only; it changes no physical postulate, adopted constant c, trajectory, force or interaction. No omitted expression or qualitative smallness choice replaces a quantitative step.

items.title: Specified low-speed momentum-energy correspondence between the relativistic measured quantities and the Newtonian comparison quantities
items.reference: scaffold/special-relativity.md SR11 reservation ("pthm specified p/E correspondence"; closure "baseline M08; Q4 controlled correspondence"); scaffold/mathematical-prerequisites.md#M08
items.design_state: complete conditional deduction of the uniform correspondence from the adopted momentum/measurement postulate and the pair's uniform expansion lemma; constants depend on the speed bound
items.physical_scope: Flat special-relativity massive classical particles (constant mass m>0, P=mU) with the measured energy, spatial momentum and kinetic energy identified as E_n, q_n, T_n by post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics, in inertial frames and in the bounded low-speed domain |w|^2 <= z_0 c^2 with z_0<1, in the SI conventions. The error bounds are uniform on that domain and depend on z_0; nothing is asserted uniformly as |w| -> c. Excludes massless particles, variable mass, forces, interactions and interactions mechanisms, accelerated observers, gravity, quantum and statistical descriptions, and every empirical claim, measurement value or precision statement.
items.statement:
Adopt [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]] (massive-particle momentum, the identification of measured quantities and isolated collision balance) and the SI conventions of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]]. Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the affine Minkowski model, $c>0$, let $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ be an inertial frame with stationary observer $n:=e_0$, spatial Euclidean structure $(S,\delta,|\cdot|)$ and inertial chart $x$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]), and let a massive particle have constant mass $m>0$ and four-momentum $P=mU$ with $U$ future timelike, $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$. Let $y$ be a worldline of the particle whose inertial coordinate path is $t\mapsto(ct,r(t))$ and whose coordinate velocity $w(t)=r'(t)\in S$ of [[def-sr-newtonian-comparison-quantities]]\,(b) equals a fixed $w$ at the instant considered; then in this frame $P=m\gamma_w(c,w)$ with $\gamma_w=(1-|w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$ ([[lem-sr-four-momentum-in-inertial-frame]]\,(b), [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(e)).

Fix $z_0\in[0,1)$ and suppose $z:=|w|^2/c^2\le z_0$; put $K(z_0):=\tfrac38(1-z_0)^{-5/2}$, and let $N_p(m,w)=mw$ and $N_K(m,w)=\tfrac12m|w|^2$ be the Newtonian comparison quantities of [[def-sr-newtonian-comparison-quantities]]. With $E_n(P)$, $q_n(P)$ and $T_n(P)$ the measured energy, spatial momentum and kinetic energy identified in clause (ii) of the adopted postulate, $m(P)$ the invariant mass of [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]] and $R_E,R_q$ the remainders of [[lem-sr-uniform-low-speed-expansion-of-observer-quantities]]:

(a) [Energy] $E_n(P)=mc^2+N_K(m,w)+R_E$ and $E_n(P)-T_n(P)=mc^2$; $|R_E|\le K(z_0)\,z\,m|w|^2$. So the measured energy of the moving particle exceeds its rest energy by the Newtonian kinetic energy up to the displayed uniform bound of order $m|w|^4/c^2$.

(b) [Kinetic energy] $T_n(P)=N_K(m,w)+R_E$, hence $|T_n(P)-N_K(m,w)|\le 2K(z_0)\,z\,N_K(m,w)$: for $w\ne0$ the relative deviation from the Newtonian kinetic energy is at most $2K(z_0)z$.

(c) [Momentum] $q_n(P)=N_p(m,w)+R_q$, and $|R_q|\le\bigl(\tfrac12+K(z_0)z_0\bigr)z\,|N_p(m,w)|$; for $w\ne0$ the relative deviation from the Newtonian momentum is at most $(\tfrac12+K(z_0)z_0)z$.

(d) [Momentum-to-velocity inversion] $w=q_n(P)/(m\gamma_w)$ exactly, and $|w-q_n(P)/m|=(\gamma_w-1)|w|\le\bigl(\tfrac12+K(z_0)z_0\bigr)z\,|w|$; at $z=0$ one has $w=0$, $q_n(P)=0$, $E_n(P)=mc^2$ and $T_n(P)=0$, and $m(P)=m$ always.

(e) [Scope and uniformity] The constants $K(z_0)$ and $\tfrac12+K(z_0)z_0$ depend on $z_0$ alone, so the estimates hold uniformly over all masses $m>0$, all states, instants and inertial frames with $|w|^2\le z_0c^2$. The statement is a conditional correspondence between the model's adopted measured quantities and the comparison functionals of a named frame: it identifies no framework with another, asserts no convergence of trajectories, forces or interactions and no limit in which the constant $c$ varies, gives no bound uniform in $|w|<c$ (see [[rem-sr-newtonian-bridge-limits-and-failures]]) and makes no empirical claim.
items.strategy:
The deduction is the transport of [[lem-sr-uniform-low-speed-expansion-of-observer-quantities]] through the adopted identification of measured quantities. By clause (ii) of [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]] the measured energy, spatial momentum and kinetic energy of the particle are $E_n(P)$, $q_n(P)$ and $T_n(P)$, and by clause (i) the particle's four-momentum is $P=mU$ with $m>0$ constant; the SI units of the comparison functionals and of $E_n,q_n,T_n$ are those of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]]. The frame data identify the state's relative velocity with the coordinate velocity: clause (e) of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] states that for the frame's stationary observer $n=e_0$ the relative velocity of clause (d) is the coordinate velocity $w$, and clause (b) of [[lem-sr-four-momentum-in-inertial-frame]] gives the components $P=m\gamma_w(c,w)$ with $\gamma_w=(1-|w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$.

Under the hypothesis $z=|w|^2/c^2\le z_0$, the batch lemma gives $E_n(P)=mc^2+\tfrac12m|w|^2+R_E$, $T_n(P)=\tfrac12m|w|^2+R_E$ and $q_n(P)=mw+R_q$ with the displayed bounds, and $R_E,R_q$ depend on the state only through $z$, $m$, $|w|$ and the constants $K(z_0)$; clause (a) is exactly this substitution together with the definition $T_n=E_n-mc^2$ and the postulate's identification of $mc^2$ as the rest energy, clause(b) retains the absolute bound also at w=0, and divides by the positive $N_K=\tfrac12m|w|^2$ only when w is nonzero, clause(c) divides by the positive $|N_p|=m|w|$ only when w is nonzero, and clause (d) uses $q_n=m\gamma_ww$ so that $w-q_n/m=(1-\gamma_w)w$, hence $|w-q_n/m|=(\gamma_w-1)|w|$ with $|\gamma_w-1|$ bounded as in the Taylor lemma. Clause (e) records that no step used more than $z\le z_0$, and that no claim beyond the stated class follows: the bounds are conditional, and the failure of any speed-independent constant is exhibited in [[rem-sr-newtonian-bridge-limits-and-failures]] and on the companion example page.

items.title: Limits of the Newtonian bridge: speed-dependent error constants, the excluded massless case, and bounded chart regions
items.reference: scaffold/special-relativity.md SR11 reservation ("rem failure at relativistic/null speeds"); prose-scaffold.md SR11 row ("not a universal cross-framework identification")
items.design_state: scope remark recording the three failure modes as consequences of the cited displayed identities
items.physical_scope: Scope remark for the flat special-relativity massive-particle model and the same bounded low-speed domain as pthm-sr-newtonian-p-e-correspondence: it records the failure of any speed-independent error constant as |w| -> c, the exclusion of ideal massless particles, and the Galilean chart limit on bounded regions and its whole-domain failure for nonzero boost velocity (the zero-velocity maps coincide everywhere). It asserts no new physical law, no dynamics, and no empirical statement.
items.statement:
Scope remark on the limits of the low-speed bridge. Each quantitative assertion is an immediate consequence of the cited displayed identities; none of them is used as a premise elsewhere on this page.

(i) [No speed-independent error constant] Let $m>0$. For every $B\ge0$ there are a future unit $n\in V$, a vector $U$ with $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ and a state $P=mU$ whose relative velocity $w$ of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(d) satisfies $|w|<c$ and $\bigl|T_n(P)-\tfrac12m|w|^2\bigr|>B$, with $T_n$ as in [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]]. Explicitly, for every integer $\gamma\ge2$ there is such a state with Lorentz factor $\gamma$, namely $|w|=c\sqrt{1-\gamma^{-2}}$, for which [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(b) gives $T_n(P)=mc^2(\gamma-1)$ while $\tfrac12m|w|^2=\tfrac12mc^2(1-\gamma^{-2})$, so $$T_n(P)-\tfrac12m|w|^2=mc^2\Bigl(\gamma-\tfrac32+\tfrac{1}{2\gamma^2}\Bigr)\to\infty\quad(\gamma\to\infty),$$ and the relative deviation from the Newtonian value equals $\frac{(2\gamma+1)(\gamma-1)}{\gamma+1}\to\infty$. Consequently the constants $K(z_0)$ and $\tfrac12+K(z_0)z_0$ of [[pthm-sr-newtonian-p-e-correspondence]] necessarily depend on the speed bound $z_0$, no bound of that form is uniform on the whole domain $|w|<c$, and $E_n(P)=mc^2\gamma$ and $|q_n(P)|=mc\sqrt{\gamma^2-1}$ are unbounded as $|w|\to c$ although $\tfrac12m|w|^2\le\tfrac12mc^2$ there.

(ii) [The massless case is excluded, not a limit] An ideal massless particle of [[post-sr-ideal-massless-particle-momentum]] carries a nonzero future null four-momentum $P$ and, by [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(a)(i), satisfies $E_n(P)=c|q_n(P)|>0$ exactly; it has no four-velocity, proper time or relative velocity, and no rest mass, rest energy or kinetic energy is assigned to it. The hypotheses $m>0$ and $z\le z_0<1$ exclude it, and no substitution $w$ with $|w|=c$ is available because $\gamma_w$ is undefined there. The bridge therefore concerns massive particles only, and it neither derives nor constrains the ideal massless case or light.

(iii) [Bounded chart regions, not a limit of frameworks] For fixed $v\in S$, the uniform chart statement [[lem-sr-uniform-galilean-limit-of-boost-charts]] holds on each bounded region $D_{T,R}$ as $C\to\infty$ (its clause (c)). For $v\ne0$ it fails on the whole chart domain $\mathbb R\times S$ (its clause (d)); for $v=0$, $\Phi_{0,C}=G_0=\mathrm{id}$ for every $C>0$, so convergence is uniform on the whole chart domain. The nonzero-velocity failure does not assert failure on every unbounded subset; the correspondence is a conditional statement about the adopted model in a bounded low-speed domain, and it is neither an equivalence between the relativistic and Newtonian frameworks, nor a physical process in which the constant $c$ varies, nor empirical evidence for either framework. The Newtonian comparison quantities [[def-sr-newtonian-comparison-quantities]] are comparison expressions, not the derived quantities of a separate theory.
items.strategy: A scope remark whose clauses are the displayed consequences of earlier items, recorded without proof obligations. (i) For each integer $\gamma\ge2$ one has $\sqrt{1-\gamma^{-2}}<1$; taking $w$ of that rescaled norm in $n^\perp$ and $U=c\gamma(n+w/c)$ gives $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ by [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(d), and [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(b) supplies $T_n(P)=mc^2(\gamma-1)$ and $|w|^2=c^2(1-\gamma^{-2})$; the displayed difference and its ratio $\frac{(2\gamma+1)(\gamma-1)}{\gamma+1}$ are elementary algebra in $\mathbb R$ ([[def-rational-power]] conventions for the exponents). Since $\gamma$ is arbitrary, no real $B$ bounds the difference uniformly, which is exactly the claim that the constant of the correspondence must depend on $z_0$. (ii) Repeats the defining exclusions of [[post-sr-ideal-massless-particle-momentum]] and the null identity of the batch-8 lemma; there is no new claim. (iii) Repeats bounded-region convergence in clause (c) of the chart lemma, whole-domain failure for v!=0 in clause (d), and identity of both maps for v=0 in clause (a); it makes no failure claim for every unbounded subset. The correspondence theorem clause (e) supplies the conditional framework scope. Fix n and a unit e in its rest space once, and take w=c sqrt(1−gamma^−2)e. Then −eta(U/c,n)=gamma exactly. For any B>=0, thm-of-archimedean supplies an integer gamma>max(2,B/(mc²)+3/2); the displayed difference is greater than mc²(gamma−3/2)>B. The relative ratio exceeds gamma−1 and is unbounded by the same Archimedean property. No sequence of independently chosen unit vectors or additional choice premise is needed.

items.title: Worked low-speed correspondence at $|w|=c/5$
items.design_state: exact radical computations with rounded decimals and a check of every displayed bound
items.physical_scope: Numerical specialisation of pthm-sr-newtonian-p-e-correspondence for a single massive particle state with |w|=c/5 in a named inertial frame of the flat model, in SI conventions. The displayed decimals are rounded values of exact radical expressions, not measurements; no experimental value, uncertainty or precision claim is made, and no other state or frame is covered.
items.statement:
Specialise [[pthm-sr-newtonian-p-e-correspondence]] to one massive particle of mass $m>0$ whose coordinate velocity $w$ in a named inertial frame satisfies $|w|/c=1/5$, so that $z=1/25$ and $z_0=z$. Then $\gamma_w=(1-1/25)^{-1/2}=5/\sqrt{24}=5\sqrt6/12\approx1.0206207262$ and $K(z_0)=\tfrac38(25/24)^{5/2}\approx0.4152916366$ ([[def-rational-power]], [[lem-rational-power-laws]]); all decimals below are rounded and all inequalities are between the exact expressions.

(a) [Rate of the expansion at $z=1/25$] $\gamma_w-1-\tfrac z2=5\sqrt6/12-51/50\approx0.0006207262$, while the bound of [[lem-sr-uniform-low-speed-taylor-remainder]] is $K(z_0)z^2=\tfrac38(25/24)^{5/2}/625\approx0.0006644666$, so the remainder bound holds and is sharp to about $7\%$ here.

(b) [Energy and kinetic energy] $E_n(P)-mc^2=mc^2(5\sqrt6/12-1)\approx0.0206207262\,mc^2$ while $N_K(m,w)=\tfrac1{50}mc^2=0.02\,mc^2$; the deviation $\approx0.0006207262\,mc^2$ obeys the bound $K(z_0)z\,m|w|^2=mc^2K(z_0)z^2\approx0.0006644666\,mc^2$ (all in units of $mc^2$).

(c) [Momentum] $|q_n(P)|=m\gamma_w|w|=\tfrac{\sqrt6}{12}mc\approx0.2041241452\,mc$ while $|N_p(m,w)|=mc/5=0.2\,mc$; the deviation is $\approx0.0041241452\,mc$ against the bound $(\tfrac12+K(z_0)z)z\,mc/5=(0.5+0.0166116655)\cdot0.04\,mc/5\approx0.0041328933\,mc$.

(d) [Momentum-to-velocity inversion] $|w-q_n(P)/m|/|w|=\gamma_w-1=5\sqrt6/12-1\approx0.0206207262$, within the bound $(\tfrac12+K(z_0)z)z\approx0.0206644666$ of clause (d) of the theorem.

The state is admissible: $z=1/25<1$, and $w$ of norm $c/5$ is realized in a frame chart by the hypothesis; the case $|w|=c$ is not considered, and the numbers carry no empirical content.
items.strategy: (a) Substitution of $z=1/25$ in [[lem-sr-uniform-low-speed-taylor-remainder]]\,(b), with the exact value $\gamma_w=(24/25)^{-1/2}=(25/24)^{1/2}=5/\sqrt{24}=5\sqrt6/12$ computed through [[lem-rational-power-laws]] ($(a/b)^{1/2}=a^{1/2}b^{-1/2}$); the displayed decimals are rounded to the displayed decimal places. (b) and (c) substitute $|w|=c/5$ and $\gamma_w=5\sqrt6/12$ into clauses (a)-(c) of [[pthm-sr-newtonian-p-e-correspondence]], whose premises (the adopted postulate and the frame data) hold by hypothesis; the comparison quantities are $N_K=mc^2/50$ and $|N_p|=mc/5$ from [[def-sr-newtonian-comparison-quantities]]. (d) Uses $w-q_n(P)/m=(1-\gamma_w)w$ from [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(b) and the bound of the theorem's clause (d). The inequality checks are arithmetic comparisons of the displayed exact expressions; the rounded decimals are computational illustrations only.

items.title: Worked uniform Galilean chart bound on a bounded region
items.reference: scaffold/special-relativity.md SR11 reservation ("explicit Galilean limiting chart maps with bounded domains")
items.design_state: explicit numerical instance of the exact differences, the uniform bounds and the epsilon choice
items.statement:
Take $v=e_1$ (so $|v|=1$), $T=1$, $R=2$ and the point $(t,x)=(1,2e_1)$ in [[def-sr-galilean-limiting-charts]], and let $\Phi_{v,C}(1,2e_1)=(t',x')$. Then for $C=10$: $\gamma_C=(99/100)^{-1/2}=10/\sqrt{99}=10/(3\sqrt{11})\approx1.0050378153$, $t'\approx0.9849370590$, $x'\approx1.0050378153$, so with the Galilean value $G_v(1,2e_1)=(1,e_1)$,
$$|t'-t|\approx0.0150629410\le(\gamma_C-1)T+\gamma_C\tfrac{|v|R}{C^2}\approx0.0251385716,$$ $$|x'-(x-tv)|\approx0.0050378153\le(\gamma_C-1)(R+|v|T)\approx0.0151134458 ;$$ for $C=100$ the same quantities are $\gamma_C\approx1.0000500038$, $|t'-t|\approx0.0001500063\le0.0002500138$ and $|x'-(x-tv)|\approx0.0000500038\le0.0001500113$. The observed deviations shrink by the factors $\approx100.4$ and $\approx100.7$ when $C$ grows from $10$ to $100$, consistent with the explicit $O(1/C^2)$ rate of [[lem-sr-uniform-galilean-limit-of-boost-charts]]\,(c). The ratios of the exact deviations, evaluated before rounding, are approximately 100.4154227043 and 100.7487483984, respectively. Finally, for tolerance $\varepsilon=0.01$, take $z_0=1/4$. Then $K_0=4\sqrt3/9$ and $A_0=1/2+\sqrt3/9<3/4$. Choose exactly $z_1=1/900$. With $H=T+R+|v|T=4$, one has $z_1<z_0$, $A_0z_1<1/1200<1/2$ and $A_0Hz_1<1/300<\varepsilon/2=1/200$, so every threshold inequality is satisfied. The sufficient threshold is $$C_\varepsilon=\max\{1/\sqrt{z_1},\sqrt{3|v|R/\varepsilon}\}=\max\{30,\sqrt{600}\}=30>1=|v|.$$ Thus $C=30$ is sufficient uniformly on $D_{1,2}$. At the specified point $\gamma_{30}=30/\sqrt{899}$, $|t'-t|=1-449/(15\sqrt{899})\approx0.0016674389$ and $|x'-(x-tv)|=30/\sqrt{899}-1\approx0.0005560189$, both below $0.01$. The whole-region bound values at $C=30$ are approximately $0.0027794768$ and $0.0016680568$, also below $0.01$. All displayed decimals are rounded to ten places after the decimal point and all inequalities compare exact values. No physical interpretation of the auxiliary $\Phi_{v,C}$ family is asserted.
items.strategy: With delta(e1,2e1)=2 and |v|=1, put g_C=C/sqrt(C^2-1). The definition gives gamma_C=g_C, t'=(C^2-2)/(C sqrt(C^2-1)) and x'=g_C e1; the Galilean value is (1,e1). At C=10,30,100, t'<1: both sides are positive, and (C^2-2)^2<C^2(C^2-1) is equivalent to 4<3C^2. Thus the exact deviations are d_t(C)=1-(C^2-2)/(C sqrt(C^2-1)) and d_x(C)=C/sqrt(C^2-1)-1. The exact uniform bound values from lemma(b) are B_t(C)=C/sqrt(C^2-1)-1+2/(C sqrt(C^2-1)) and B_x(C)=3(C/sqrt(C^2-1)-1). Evaluate these exact radical expressions at the three scales, then round to ten places after the decimal point. Ratios are evaluated from the exact radical expressions, not already rounded deviations: d_t(10)/d_t(100)=100.4154227043 to ten decimal places and d_x(10)/d_x(100)=100.7487483984 to ten decimal places, hence 100.4 and 100.7 to one decimal place. For the tolerance proof, z0=1/4 gives K0=(3/8)(3/4)^(-5/2)=4sqrt(3)/9 and A0=1/2+sqrt(3)/9<3/4, since sqrt(3)<9/4 follows by squaring the positive quantities: 3<81/16. Therefore z1=1/900 is positive, <=z0, A0 z1<1/1200<1/2 and A0 H z1<1/300<1/200=epsilon/2. This proves z1<=min{z0,1/(2A0),epsilon/(2A0H)} explicitly. The sufficient threshold is |v|/sqrt(z1)=30, while sqrt(3|v|R/epsilon)=sqrt(600)<30 because 600<900; hence C_epsilon=30>|v|. The lemma therefore controls both errors uniformly on the entire bounded region. Exact radical evaluation gives the stated point and bound values at C=30. No ellipsis or empirical claim is used, and the fixed model scale c is not varied.

items.title: Counterexample: no speed-independent uniform low-speed remainder for the kinetic energy
items.reference: scaffold/special-relativity.md SR11 reservation ("rem failure at relativistic/null speeds"); scaffold/mathematical-prerequisites.md#M08 ("constants depend on z_0")
items.design_state: complete refutation by the explicit family gamma = n with the exact difference formula
items.statement:
**Statement refuted.** Let $c>0$ and $m>0$. There is a real $B\ge0$ such that $|T_n(P)-\tfrac12m|w|^2|\le B$ for every future unit $n\in V$, every $P=mU$ with $U$ future timelike and $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$, and the relative velocity $w$ of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(d), where $T_n$ is the kinetic energy of [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]].

**Counterexample.** Fix a future unit $n$ and a unit vector $e\in n^\perp$ once; for every integer $N\ge2$ use that same vector (possible because $n^\perp$ is a three-dimensional real subspace on which the restriction of $\eta$ is positive definite, so every nonzero vector of $n^\perp$ may be divided by its norm, [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(c)) and put $$w_N:=c\sqrt{1-N^{-2}}\;e,\qquad U_N:=cN\Bigl(n+\frac{w_N}{c}\Bigr),\qquad P_N:=mU_N .$$ Then $|w_N|^2=c^2(1-N^{-2})<c^2$, and $\eta(U_N,U_N)=c^2N^2(-1+|w_N|^2/c^2)=-c^2$ with $U_N$ future timelike, so $U_N$ has the required four-velocity normalization; $u_N=U_N/c$ is future unit timelike; the relative velocity and Lorentz factor of $U_N$ are $w_N$ and $N$, and [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(b) gives $T_n(P_N)=mc^2(N-1)$ together with $\tfrac12m|w_N|^2=\tfrac12mc^2(1-N^{-2})$. Hence $$T_n(P_N)-\tfrac12m|w_N|^2=mc^2\Bigl(N-\tfrac32+\tfrac1{2N^2}\Bigr),$$ which exceeds any prescribed real $B$ for all sufficiently large $N$; equivalently the relative deviation $\frac{T_n(P_N)-\frac12m|w_N|^2}{\frac12m|w_N|^2}=\frac{(2N+1)(N-1)}{N+1}$ is unbounded in $N$. Therefore the refuted statement is false for every pair $(c,m)$, and any valid low-speed error bound must depend on the admissible speed domain (the constants $K(z_0)$ of [[pthm-sr-newtonian-p-e-correspondence]] do). The construction is a statement about the stipulated model and contains no empirical claim.
items.strategy: Assume the refuted statement and derive a contradiction. Fix a future unit $n$ and $e\in n^\perp$ with $|e|=1$; for each $N\ge2$ set $a_N:=c\sqrt{1-N^{-2}}$, $w_N:=a_Ne$ and $U_N:=cN(n+w_N/c)$. By [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(c) $\eta(n,w_N)=0$ and $\eta(w_N,w_N)=a_N^2$, so $\eta(U_N,U_N)=c^2N^2(\eta(n,n)+2\eta(n,w_N)/c+\eta(w_N,w_N)/c^2)=c^2N^2(-1+a_N^2/c^2)=-c^2$, and $U_N$ is future timelike; clause (d) of the same theorem then identifies $w_N=h(U_N)/\gamma=c\,h(U_N/c)/\gamma$ with $\gamma=N$, because $\gamma=-\eta(U_N/c,n)=N$. Applying [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(b) to $P_N=mU_N$ gives $T_n(P_N)=mc^2(N-1)$, $|w_N|^2=c^2(1-N^{-2})$ and the displayed difference; the relative deviation is the quotient of these expressions, namely $\frac{(2N+1)(N-1)}{N+1}$ (verified by multiplying out). Since $N-\tfrac32+\tfrac1{2N^2}\to\infty$ as $N\to\infty$ in the ordered field $\mathbb R$ ([[def-rational-power]], [[lem-of-abs-value]] conventions), for every real $B$ there is $N$ with $mc^2(N-\tfrac32+\tfrac1{2N^2})>B$, contradicting the assumed uniform bound. The norms and the causality classification are those of [[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]] and [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]] for the model [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]. More explicitly choose a canonical integer N>max(2,B/(mc²)+3/2) using thm-of-archimedean. The displayed absolute difference is greater than mc²(N−3/2)>B, and the relative ratio exceeds N−1. This closes both unboundedness assertions by the exact published real-field supplier rather than an unspecified limit argument.
